original_query: select    cd_gender,   cd_marital_status,   cd_education_status,   count(*) cnt1,   cd_purchase_estimate,   count(*) cnt2,   cd_credit_rating,   count(*) cnt3  from   customer c,customer_address ca,customer_demographics  where   c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk and   ca_state in ('IN','NM','VA') and   cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk   and cd_marital_status in ('W', 'S', 'M')   and cd_education_status in ('Secondary', 'Primary') and   exists (select *           from store_sales,date_dim           where c.c_customer_sk = ss_customer_sk and                 ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                 d_year = 2000 and                 d_moy between 9 and 9+2                 and ss_list_price between 5 and 94           ) and    (not exists (select *             from web_sales,date_dim             where c.c_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk and                   ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                   d_year = 2000 and                   d_moy between 9 and 9+2                   and ws_list_price between 5 and 94             ) and     not exists (select *             from catalog_sales,date_dim             where c.c_customer_sk = cs_ship_customer_sk and                   cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                   d_year = 2000 and                   d_moy between 9 and 9+2                   and cs_list_price between 5 and 94)             )  group by cd_gender,           cd_marital_status,           cd_education_status,           cd_purchase_estimate,           cd_credit_rating  order by cd_gender,           cd_marital_status,           cd_education_status,           cd_purchase_estimate,           cd_credit_rating  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
select cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, count(*) cnt1, cd_purchase_estimate, count(*) cnt2, cd_credit_rating, count(*) cnt3
from customer c, customer_address ca, customer_demographics
where c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
  and ca_state in ('IN','NM','VA')
  and cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
  and cd_marital_status in ('W', 'S', 'M')
  and cd_education_status in ('Secondary', 'Primary')
  and exists (select 1
              from store_sales, date_dim
              where c.c_customer_sk = ss_customer_sk
                and ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
                and d_year = 2000
                and d_moy between 9 and 11
                and ss_list_price between 5 and 94)
  and (not exists (select 1
                   from web_sales, date_dim
                   where c.c_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk
                     and ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
                     and d_year = 2000
                     and d_moy between 9 and 11
                     and ws_list_price between 5 and 94)
       and not exists (select 1
                       from catalog_sales, date_dim
                       where c.c_customer_sk = cs_ship_customer_sk
                         and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
                         and d_year = 2000
                         and d_moy between 9 and 11
                         and cs_list_price between 5 and 94))
group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
order by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Folded 'd_moy between 9 and 9+2' into 'd_moy between 9 and 11' in all three subqueries for clarity; optimizer folds this anyway so no plan change.

Changed 'select *' to 'select 1' in EXISTS/NOT EXISTS subqueries (cosmetic only). Correlated EXISTS/NOT EXISTS forms were preserved because the previous CTE-hoisted rewrite regressed cost from ~132k to ~306k by replacing per-customer index probes with bulk hash joins; date_dim is tiny (73k rows) so hoisting/materializing it is counterproductive.

No CTE was introduced. Given data statistics (large fact tables: store_sales 28.8M, web_sales 7.2M, catalog_sales 14.4M vs. small filtered customer_address ~3 rows per state and tiny date filter), the original plan's semi/anti-join with index probes is optimal. Repeated count(*) aliases are deduplicated by the planner and left untouched. No further equivalent rewrite is expected to improve the plan.
